qualifying_updates.title: The Manipulated Agent: When Apify's MCP Turns Against You
qualifying_updates.author: Eitan Chassid and Yotam Perkal
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Direct page date visible under the author names.
qualifying_updates.summary: Pluto Security describes an indirect prompt-injection scenario where untrusted web content returned through an MCP server can steer an authenticated follow-up action. The article recommends separating open-web retrieval from authenticated state-changing tools, preserving provenance for tool arguments, requiring confirmation for new destinations or destructive/spend actions, and monitoring chains of context and tool calls rather than isolated calls.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a local retrieval-and-tools and governance update because it gives concrete architecture rules for MCP trust boundaries, source provenance, approvals, and prompt-injection-resistant tool-call workflows.

qualifying_updates.author: Andrew Stiefel
qualifying_updates.visible_date: Published on August 31, 2026; Updated on August 31, 2026
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Direct published and updated dates visible in the article header.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article argues that AI-native code analysis should be evaluated by operational outcomes such as whether the security-debt backlog becomes smaller, younger, and cheaper to remediate. qualifying_updates.title: The AI-Native SDLC Starts With Your Infrastructure
qualifying_updates.author: Eyal Bukchin
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Direct page date visible next to the author name.
qualifying_updates.summary: The article responds to an agentic SDLC playbook by arguing that agent verification depends on what the agent's code actually runs against. It distinguishes file artifacts such as intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, CLAUDE.md, skills, and REVIEW.md from runtime reality, and recommends production-like dependency access plus isolation for concurrent agent sessions through traffic filtering, queue splitting, and database branching.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a local verification, context-architecture, and application-patterns update because it treats agent self-checks as environment-dependent and calls out shared staging interference when several agents test at once.
